newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia PGM metal export possible end Mar/early Apr.
newsitem.headline: Russia PGM metal export possible end Mar/early Apr.

text.p: Russian deliveries of palladium and platinum to Japan may start at the end of March or the beginning of April, the deputy chief executive of state precious metals export agency Almazjuvelirexport said on Thursday.
"It's fully possible at the end of March or the beginning of April," Alexander Kulichkov told Reuters, when asked when exports could start, adding, "it's more possible than not possible."
He said that the start of exports hinged on a resolution awaiting signature by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
"We're waiting for the government order," Kulichkov said. "I think the text of it is ready. We made our recommendations to the Finance Ministry (on the contents of the order) and they were accepted."
But he said Almazjuvelirexport would not lobby the government to process the document and that he did not know when Chernomyrdin might sign the order, which would authorise the stalled exports.
"We don't lobby; we just fulfil state orders, because we are a state organisation," he said.
Kulichkov said he was aware that markets were awaiting clarity on when deliveries might begin.
"Everybody is worried and the market is nervous. We're all waiting," he said.
He said the agency was in contact with Japanese buyers but gave no further details.
Japan is the world's leading consumer of palladium and Russia is the world's largest palladium supplier and a leading exporter of platinum.
